comments.body:
Fix review: merge bf2a7c9711c68ef5e61fbb4a25c9f16a3ddd488b

Round-2 DELTA review of the repaired W3 solver-knob fix, from my own detached
worktree `/tmp/audit-5/review/w3-search-delta/wt` (a `git worktree add --detach`
of the head). Measured at `bf2a7c9711c68ef5e61fbb4a25c9f16a3ddd488b`, which is
the live head (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/fix/r5-w3-search` -> this SHA)
and the SHA the body names. Every arm of the round-1 block (`bb1fe25b`) is
closed, and I could not find anything to re-block on. Evidence under
`/tmp/audit-5/review/w3-search-delta/`.

## The block is closed, arm by arm

1. **#1294 is genuinely gone.** `_MULTI_START_SOLVES = 4` at the head and at
   the merge base `9ca86655`; `_MULTI_START_SOLVES = 6` appears nowhere in the
   tree. The whole production diff against the merge base is the #1295
   warm-start hunk: `coordinator._warm_seeded` (its `_prev_shipped_plan`
   assignment at `coordinator.py:1238` is the only production writer) wired into
   `_solve_snapshot`, and `optimizer._warm_start_starts` called once as
   `_solve(self._warm_start_starts(n_steps))`. No bang-bang seed or
   refine-cut literal survives. Sweep is GREEN: `131.10x` in the gate and
   `133.31x` on the standalone re-run, both under the `134.32x` budget.

2. **The #1295 check is genuinely BLAS-robust — no pinned float, no absolute %.**
   The three new checks in `tests/optimality.py` are:
   - the candidate-count check: `len(warm)==len(cold)+1`, `array_equal(warm[0],
     handed_plan)`, and the structural tail equal. Counts and array equality,
     not a solve float; the structural candidates are pure functions of the
     inputs (`starts = list(h.extra_starts) + starts` prepends the handed plan),
     so the count is machine-independent. This is the discriminator.
   - the no-worse check: `_j15w <= _j15f * (1 + 1e-9)` — a DIRECTIONAL band
     (the invariant that a candidate added to the set cannot raise the minimum),
     exactly what round 1 asked for in place of the absolute percentage. On this
     box both arms read `12.4354`; a `+/-1%` float machine still satisfies it
     because the handed plan IS the cold optimum, so the warm arm's minimum
     cannot exceed the cold arm's whatever the floats do.
   - the wrong-width null: two independent solves of the same code path compared
     with `np.array_equal` — exact on any BLAS (`0.286541` both ways here).

3. **The claims are clean.** `env_drift.py --all 9ca86655` -> `NO UNCLAIMED
   DRIFT: 56` and `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56`, exit 0 (no `capacity_tariff` /
   `cool_rainy_summer` movers, which were #1294's and left with it).
   `--claims-only 9ca86655` -> `claims hygiene: ... ok`, exit 0. The bare list
   in `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` is empty (the three #1294 claims are
   gone; the R5-D2-02 baseline line is removed and its note kept). The card file
   is byte-identical to the merge base and this branch touches no card source.

4. **Null controls and suites at the head.** `ALL 18 OPTIMALITY CHECKS PASSED`;
   `ALL 3065 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` with `tests/features.py` a 0-line diff
   against the merge base (the flat-fee null control is a real null again);
   `ALL 1674 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`; `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; `ALL 77 STRESS
   CHECKS PASSED` (see the caveat below); scoped gate `MODE: SCOPED -- 20
   script(s) run, 4 scoped out` matching the body's four (`frontend`,
   `ha_contract`, `harness_headers`, `open_meteo`); `prepr.sh <body> 1295` ->
   `clean / no refusal`, `pr-body 0 error(s)`, `figures 13 resolved, 1 not
   verified (unverifiable by design), 0 refused`. VERSION, `manifest.json` and
   the notes heading are untouched (`6.6.8` == the manifest version ==
   `claims-for:`); `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0 (the
   `claimnotes` driver is installed).

5. **The mutation proof reddens exactly one check.** `M3_warm_none` (revert
   `_warm_start_starts` to `None`) -> `1 of 18 OPTIMALITY CHECKS FAILED`, the
   named check being the candidate-count check, with `cold [4], warm [4]`. The
   no-worse arm and the width null do NOT move, which is correct: the no-worse
   arm is an invariant and is documented as one, not offered as a discriminator.

The round-1 section-4 carry is also closed: `.claude/workflows/carry-1295.json`
is in the diff and lints clean (`brief_lint.mjs` -> `TOTAL: 0 error(s)`, exit 0).
The round-1 section-2 disposition is preserved: `refute_1293.py` is committed
and `tests/backtest.py` reads `ALL 25 BACKTEST CHECKS PASSED` (shoulder optimizer
`4.44` vs night tariff `4.48`), so #1293 stays refuted.

## One caveat, reported not charged

On my first (contended) pass, `tests/stress.py` read `1 of 77` — but on the
**pre-existing** round-5 D9-07 per-call kernel-CPU instrument self-test, not the
sweep: it injects a 2x per-call seam cost and requires the ratio to clear the
`1.80x` `SCENARIO_KERNEL_FACTOR`, and the arm read `x1.68` (`42 ms -> 71 ms`).
On a quiet re-run with the gate lease held, the same armed check PASSES and the
sweep reads `ALL 77 STRESS CHECKS PASSED`. The box carried a system process
(`ANECompilerService`) pinning a core at 99.5% and a 15-min load average of
~11 during the first run. `tests/stress.py` is a 0-line diff against the merge
base, the branch adds no per-call kernel cost, and the sweep's own ledger reads
`0 re-planned by this branch` — so this is instrument flake under contention,
not this branch's defect, and not a re-block. Worth a note for D9: the D9-07
self-test's 2x injection has only ~11% margin over its 1.80x factor
(`2.0/1.80`), the same razor the surrounding comments already flag, and it can
false-red a loaded box.

Local-only: I did not push, and did not open or comment on any PR or issue. I
could not read CI check-runs (no `gh` for this head here), so the BLAS-robustness
above is established from the code and my own runs, not from the runner.

WHAT I RAN, ARM BY ARM

1. Mutation proof, in my own mutant worktree (`/valved/mut`), overwriting only
   `thermal_model.py` with 67d91389's copy (SHA-256 0236e772… == `git show
   67d91389:…`, so the revert is byte-exact and touches nothing else; the diff is
   1 file, +10/-51). `tests/features.py` → **`1 of 3065 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`**,
   the single FAIL being the named check *"more power never leaves the 35 L valved
   buffer cooler [a bump cooled the buffer by -1.3052e+01 K at (0.1, 38); the
   discharge bound snaps the Euler overshoot…]"* — nothing else in the corpus
   moved. At head the same command prints `ALL 3065 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` (twice:
   standalone and inside the gate). The check is not vacuous. I also re-derived the
   three numbers in the check's own comment at the merge base: +1e-3 → -2.3218e-01,
   +0.1 → -1.3052e+01, +1.0 → -1.2975e+01 K, overall worst -1.3052e+01 at (0.1, 38)
   — matching the failure line and the comment exactly.

2. Measured with the **finder's** harness, not the fixer's. `bounds_monotone.py` is
   committed byte-identical to the finder's own export
   (/tmp/audit-5/baseline/tools/audit/round5/D2/seat-a/bounds_monotone.py) and
   carries no `live-header` marker, so `harness_headers.py` treats it as frozen
   evidence and does not execute it — the body's account of it is correct.

   -9.0523e-02 @(60,5) / -9.0523e-01 @(60,5) / -3.0325e+01 @(60,5) / -4.3465e+01
   @(33,5) at base and **0.0000e+00 at every bump at head**; the 750 L control is
   exactly 0 on both sides; `monotone_min_delta_k[valve_small]` goes -3.221e-03 at

   at both ends; `hot_tank_rate_not_state_ok=True`. Every figure in the body's
   null-control bullet reproduced exactly. The `cop_flow_carnot` ablation
   (`probe_valved.py`, run at the merge base) leaves the violation standing —
   -1.0226e-01 @81 / -4.2490e+01 @63 with the coupling off, against -9.0523e-02 @60
   / -4.3465e+01 @33 as shipped; 100 L still over the bound (-2.8280e-02 @48,
   -8.5127e+00 @69) and 750 L at 0 — so the COP curve is not the confound.
   `control_substeps.py`: only `valve_small` moves (1 → 9); the other seven families
   are 1 → 1, with the printed buffer ratios 1.509/1.509/0.402/8.621/0.402/0.402/
   0.402/0.754 matching the body digit for digit. `sweep_substeps.py` (merge-base

   `git status` clean): n_sub 1/6/7/8 non-monotone at exactly the body's values, and
   9/10/12 exactly 0, with `n_sub_measured` hitting every injected target.

3. **The 9 is the smallest clean count, and it is analytic rather than tuned.** The
   shipped buffer ratio is ua_buf·dt/C_buf = 8.6207, so ceil(8.6207/1.0) = 9; at 8

   boundary-mass `worst`), so each arm measures the residual of the real buffer draw

   `buffer_temp_trajectory[1]` 44.505886 → 32.796098 (first of 96/97 indices),
   `baseline_cost` 158.826466 → 149.153601, `deferred_energy_cost` 13.073536 →

   re-derive byte-for-byte**: applying env_drift's own `_diff_leaves` rule to the two

   `no version edit`, `rules_sync ok`, `gate mode MODE: SCOPED`. `orphan_files()` is

   non-overshoot bound: explicit Euler on dT/dt = -u(T-T∞)/C decays monotonically
   only while the factor (1 - u·dt/C) is non-negative, i.e. u·dt/C ≤ 1. The numerator
   is the right one — the throttled branch of `_simulate_step_two_zone` builds

   (1-rad_fraction)·design_power/design_dt` with `design_power =
   max_electrical_power·max(cop_nominal,1)` and `design_dt =
   max(emitter_design_delta_t,1)`, and their sum is exactly the fix's `ua_buf`; the

   sufficient for any volume, and it is conservative. The term applies only where

  export). The six other added harnesses — `control_substeps.py`,
  `probe_base_sched.py`, `probe_base_wide.py`, `probe_schedule.py`,
  `probe_valved.py`, `sweep_substeps.py` — are **the fixer's own instruments**,
  committed into the finder's seat directory with no provenance line in their
  headers and no explicit "this branch wrote it" sentence for them in the body. The
  body does mark the one finder instrument in as many words ("an instrument this
  branch did not write"). There is no misattribution — I checked each of the six
  against the finder's export and none exists there — but a later reader of
  `tools/audit/round5/D2/seat-a/` cannot tell the two sets apart. Hygiene, recorded
  so the next round's reviewer is not misled.

  including `valve_small` at 0.0000e+00. This is not a dead knob: `buffer_tank_thermal_mass`
  is a property derived from `buffer_tank_volume`, so the assignment does reach the
  counter (mass 0.0406 → 0.0464, n_sub 9 → 8, per-substep ratio 0.943 ≤ 1) — a 40 L
  valved tank is genuinely clean under the fix. Its inline rationale "(direction:
  shrink)" is wrong at the base too (the violation grew, -3.221e-03 → -2.937e-02),
  but the `EXPECTED` line's "below -1e-3 (direction: decreases)" holds and the header
  is frozen finder evidence with no `live-header` marker, so the fixer must not
  rewrite it. Correct as committed.
- Forward-carry `none` is verified rather than taken: `tools/audit/briefs/D2.md`
  line 21 (method 1) already requires "monotonicity (more power never cools a
  store)", so this finding narrows no later stage, invalidates no assumption it rests
  on and removes no option. The durable rule is in `_stability_substeps`'s docstring
  and is enforced in-tree by the new `tests/features.py` check. No wave-5 group
  covers D2, so no `carry-<N>.json` is owed.
- The body's explanation of the local stress red is verifiable and correct:
  `summer/1z/dhw/fuse-cap` is built `two_zone=False` (tests/stress.py:2211), so the
  new `buf_ratio` block is skipped, `max()` reduces to the pre-fix `worst*dt/1.5` and
  the count is arithmetically the pre-fix one; the file documents that scenario as
  the cheapest member of its class (0.3 s CPU), which is where a per-call timer sees
  ambient load first. The merges check out too: the last merge's second parent is the
  merge base, and it brought `tests/features.py` at exactly `344 insertions(+), 60
  deletions(-)` — the body's "+344/-60".
- Two docstring/hygiene nits, no action owed. (a) The divisor mirrors the step's
  `C_buf < 1e-6 → 0.04` fallback but not its `C_buf_div = max(C_buf, 0.01)` clamp;
  for a mass in [1e-6, 0.01) the counter's ratio is *larger* than the step's, i.e. it
  over-substeps — conservative only, and unreachable from the shipped configs (35 L
  → 0.0406). (b) `_stability_substeps` says an unvalved buffer "has no u·dt/C to
  bound"; true of the emitter draw, but `q_buf_loss` is a decaying coupling on the
  buffer in every mode, at a ratio of ~1.4e-3 here and unreachable at any sane loss
  coefficient. Pre-existing, and the fix only narrows the old exemption.

VERDICT

Every arm reproduces. The mutation is non-vacuous and exact, the null controls are
non-vacuous and their numbers are the body's to the digit, the divisor is the
analytic non-overshoot bound rather than a tuned constant, the golden drift is
claimed with its direction, `claims-for` equals `VERSION`, nothing else moved, the
scoped gate is green end to end under the lease, the ratchet holds with no budget
edit, `prepr` does not refuse, and the fix is provably confined to the valved
two-zone buffer (bit-identity measured on 7 of 8 families, and my own 20-config
sweep clean at head and broken at base). Merge.

ROUND 1

Dispatched as PR #1355, branch `fix/r5-pins-a`, head
`076f4a3598ea8acd193cdd2d44205b1dd8c8bb78`, base = merge base =

#1312/#1313/#1314 = R5-D3-04/-05/-06. Mid-review the PR object was re-cut:
#1355 closed, **#1361** opened on the same branch at the same head — see the
Verdict, which is where the merge is aimed.

Reviewed in a fresh detached worktree at the head SHA. Evidence, drivers and
logs: `/tmp/audit-5/review/pins-a/` (`evidence/`, `LEDGER.md`). All worktrees
were created and removed by this seat; the reviewer never pushed, never edited
the PR, never posted.

## Verdict

`merge`. Every load-bearing number in the body re-derived, under the body's own
rule; all six new pins proved non-vacuous against a live mutant, each in
isolation; the null control holds; nothing moved that should not have.

**Post this against #1361, not #1355.** #1355 was **closed unmerged** at
`2026-09-21T17:45:19Z` while this review was running; #1361 is the live re-cut,
created `17:52:30Z` from the *same* branch `fix/r5-pins-a` at the **identical**
head `076f4a3598ea8acd193cdd2d44205b1dd8c8bb78`, and the two bodies are
**byte-identical** (`diff` exit 0). The head did not move, so step 12's blocking
condition — which requires the live head to be a *different* SHA — does not
fire, and every measurement below applies to #1361 verbatim. There is nothing
to re-take and nothing to re-review; only the PR number to post against. This is
called out at the top because a merge instruction aimed at a closed pull request
would otherwise be unactionable.

## Step 1 — mutation proof (both directions)

The PR names production lines, not pins: the six checks are *new* assertions, so
"the code the PR names" is the three finder mutants the pins claim to catch. I
ran it both ways.

Mutants reproduced **verbatim** from the finder's own manifest,
`/tmp/audit-5/tmp/d3a/manifest.json` (read by id, with the manifest's own
`expect_count` occurrence assert), applied by *my* checked-edit driver
(`run_case.py`, which also fails the run if the edit leaves the file
uncompilable). Mutant identity:

- `M03` → coordinator.py `min(positives)/max(positives) if len(positives) >= 2
  else None` → `>= 200` (R5-D3-04)
- `M23` → price_model.py `return min(1.0, ...)` → `return self.quarter_days[idx]
  / QUARTER_CONFIDENCE_DAYS` (R5-D3-05)
- `M09` → coordinator.py `if not np.isfinite(thermal_kw) or thermal_kw <= 0.0:`
  → `if False and (...)` (R5-D3-06)

**Mutant applied (`tests/features.py` is the closure; see step 2):**

| run | tree | result |
|---|---|---|
| `base_all3` | base + M03+M09+M23 | **rc=0, `ALL 3044 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED`** |
| `head_all3` | head + M03+M09+M23 | **rc=1, `5 of 3050 FEATURE CHECKS FAILED`** |

Baseline reproduces the body's `ALL 3044 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` exactly (its R2);
head reproduces `5 of 3050` exactly (its R1). The five named failures and their
detail strings are **character-for-character** the ones the body quotes:

```
FAIL two published prices give the valve a price ratio
     [price_ratio=None: cheapest over dearest of [1.0, 4.0] is 0.25, and the >= 2 floor is the only thing that admits two]
FAIL quarter confidence saturates at one, however much evidence arrives
     [quarter_days=8 against a ramp of 5 reads 1.6 without the ceiling]
FAIL the damped quarter factor never overshoots the learned factor it damps
     [learned 3.265, damped 4.624 against a clip ceiling of 4.0: trust above one pushes the factor past the range the learned value is confined to]
FAIL a non-finite COP never enters the learned envelope
     [envelope={-4: [nan, 1]}: only the isfinite arm keeps NaN out, and max(NaN, x) makes it permanent]
FAIL a non-positive thermal figure never enters the learned envelope
     [envelope={-4: [-4.0, 1]}: a negative COP is not evidence of capacity either, so the <= 0.0 arm is load-bearing too]
```

`one published price is too few to state a ratio` does **not** fire on M03 — the
body discloses this and it is correct: M03 raises the floor, so the one-price
side is green under it either way.

**Pin emptied, mutant re-applied (the pins are what kill the mutants):**

| pin emptied | mutant | result |
|---|---|---|
| `vr_two` | M03 | rc=0, `ALL 3050 … PASSED` |
| `qcap_one` + `qcap_damped` | M23 | rc=0, `ALL 3050 … PASSED` |
| `qcap_one` alone | M23 | rc=1, only `…damped quarter factor…` fails |
| `qcap_damped` alone | M23 | rc=1, only `quarter confidence saturates at one…` fails |

| `env_nan` alone | M09 | rc=1, only `…non-positive thermal figure…` fails |
| `env_neg` alone | M09 | rc=1, only `…non-finite COP…` fails |

"Emptying" is a checked edit replacing the assertion expression with `True`,
leaving the `R.check` call, its name and its detail in place — so the check
count stays 3050 and the only difference is that the assertion no longer
asserts. Emptying restores the survivor in every case, and each of the four
paired pins kills its mutant **alone**: none is scenery for its neighbour.

**`vr_one` on the boundary the finder's M03 cannot reach.** The body states that
M03 leaves `vr_one` green and says the check "pins the floor's *lower* boundary,
which M03 does not move". That is an honest disclosure, but it leaves the check
unproven, so I wrote the mutant that moves that boundary —
`len(positives) >= 2` → `>= 1`, labelled `review:attack:vr_lo`, authorised by no
manifest:

| run | tree | result |
|---|---|---|
| `base_vr_lo` | **base** + `vr_lo` | rc=0, `ALL 3044 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED` |
| `head_vr_lo` | **head** + `vr_lo` | **rc=1**, exactly one failure: `one published price is too few to state a ratio` |
| `head_vr_lo_vrOneEmpty` | head + `vr_lo` + `vr_one` emptied | rc=0, `ALL 3050 … PASSED` |

So `vr_one` is not decoration. It closes a **second** unpinned mutation on the
same predicate — one the finder did not report, the fixer did not claim, and
that the baseline suite is green on — and emptying `vr_one` puts the survivor
back. All six pins are non-vacuous.

**The D3-04 pair pins the floor at exactly 2, and I checked the arithmetic of
that claim against the bracket of measured points.** The two checks read two
*coordinators*, one with two positive prices and one with one, so as functions
of the floor `f` the pair is satisfied iff (`f <= 2`, so the two-price ratio is
`0.25` and not `None`) **and** (`f >= 2`, so the one-price ratio is `None` and
not `1.0`) — that is, iff `f == 2`. The three settings the suite was actually
run at confirm both sides: `f = 2` (head, clean) → `0.25` / `None`; `f = 1`
(`vr_lo`) → `0.25` / `1.0`, so the one-price check fails and the two-price one
does not; `f = 200` (M03) → `None` / `None`, so the two-price check fails and
the one-price one does not. Upward and downward moves are each caught, by
different checks.

## Step 2 — measuring with the finder's harness, not the fixer's

The fixer disclosed that it did not run `gate_survivor.sh` once per mutant,
substituting `tests/features.py` under the same mutants plus a union closure,
and disclosed that substitution as its own instrument in the body. I do not
take that on trust, and I did not accept it silently.

**The finder's harness is not committed.** `git ls-files` at the head contains
no `tools/audit/round5/D3/seat-a/` and no `gate_survivor.sh`; the only round-5
D3 file in the tree is `tools/audit/round5/D3/seat-b/warm_pyc_miss.py`. The
harness survives only as a verbatim paste in the three issue bodies
(`/tmp/audit-5/round-runner/issues/D3-0{4,5,6}.md`). Per step 9 that is itself
a finding about the finding, and it is recorded below; it is not a defect in
this PR, which changed no harness.

**What I did instead.** I recovered the harness verbatim from those bodies and
adapted it at `/tmp/audit-5/review/pins-a/gate_survivor_head.sh`, changing four
named things and nothing else: the `cd` (this review's head worktree), `BASE`
(9f890f77 — this PR's merge base, never HEAD), the mutant set as a parameter,
and the log path. The manifest lookup, the occurrence assert, the lease
protocol, the `GATE_SCOPE=full GOLDEN_MODE=drift GOLDEN_REF=$BASE` environment
and the revert-and-check are the finder's, character for character.

I also verified the fixer's stated reason from source rather than accepting it:
`tests/features.py` is invoked unconditionally by the full gate, and the gate's
exit status is the disjunction of its scripts'.

- `tests/run.sh:347` — `run "$PYTHON" tests/features.py`, not behind any
  `in_scope` guard; it runs in `GATE_SCOPE=full`.
- `tests/run.sh:562` — `[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && failed=$((failed + 1))`, and
  `:596-598` — `if [ "$failed" -ne 0 ]; then … exit 1`.

So a red `tests/features.py` **is** a red gate, and the substitution is sound in
the only direction that matters here (it could only ever make the gate redder).
That is a proof about this gate's plumbing, not an appeal to the fixer's word,
and it is why the per-mutant table in step 1 is a gate measurement and not a
beside-the-point one.

**My own full-gate run at the head — done, and it agrees.** The attempt queued
on the box's gate lease (another seat, `fix-r5-stressgate-rev`, held it), took it
at `19:32:05 CEST`, and ran the full gate alone with no other process on the box:

```
  >>> FAILED: python3 tests/stress.py

```

```
>>> FAILED: python3 tests/stress.py
```
